title: Query executor: generated tool call -> safe, tenant/role-scoped, paginated Ecto query (no model SQL)

epic.name: Context Retriever (entity-schema -> auto-generated agent tool surface)

priority_note: The security boundary of the whole epic: it turns a model-initiated tool call into a database query. Any gap here is an injection / cross-tenant / data-exfiltration hole. Depends on the entity schema (30.1) and generator metadata (30.2).

background.reference: GitHub issue #309 ('safe, scoped Ecto query, parameterized, tenant/role-scoped, paginated. No raw SQL from the model'). Security-first.
background.includes: US-30.2 specs carry (entity, field, operation) metadata. This story executes a generated tool call against the entity's backing loopctl source, enforcing the entity allowlist, tenant scoping, role gating, parameterization, and pagination — so an agent can query structured data in one call without ever authoring SQL or reaching another tenant's rows.

story.i_want_to: execute a generated tool call by building a parameterized Ecto query scoped to the caller's tenant, restricted to the entity's allowlisted filterable/searchable fields, with enforced pagination
story.so_that: agents get governed structured-data access with no model-authored SQL, no way to filter on non-allowlisted columns, and no cross-tenant reads

rationale: This is where a model's output touches the database, so it is the highest-risk component in the epic. Building queries only from the generator's (entity, field, operation) metadata against an allowlist — never from the raw tool name or arbitrary params — plus mandatory tenant scoping and pagination is what turns 'let an LLM query our data' from a liability into a safe capability.

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.ContextRetriever.Executor.run/3 takes a scope (tenant_id + role), a generated tool spec's (entity, field, operation) metadata, and params, resolves the entity via the Registry, and builds a PARAMETERIZED Ecto query against the entity's backing loopctl source. Field/operation are validated against the entity's allowlist; a request naming a non-allowlisted field (or a field not marked filterable/searchable) is rejected, never executed.

Every query is tenant-scoped: the executor injects a tenant_id predicate (and runs on the correct repo) so results can only be the caller's tenant's rows — proven even when the backing source table also holds other tenants' data. No param can widen or override the tenant scope.

No model-authored SQL: values are always Ecto-parameterized (never string-interpolated); an injection payload in a filter value (e.g. "' OR 1=1 --") is treated as a literal value and matches nothing, not as SQL.

Pagination is enforced with a hard maximum page size (config) and returns %{results, meta: %{total_count, limit, offset}}; a caller cannot request an unbounded result set. Full-text search uses loopctl's existing Postgres full-text/keyword approach (parameterized), not raw LIKE interpolation.

Role gating: the executor (and the API in 30.4) require >= agent role to query; it also honors any per-entity/source read constraints (e.g. a source that should not expose all rows to all subjects) — documented per source in the dogfood story (30.6).
Result shaping returns only the entity's declared fields (no accidental column leakage of sensitive/undeclared columns from the backing table).

test_cases.name: filter executes as a parameterized, tenant-scoped query
preconditions: projects seeded under tenant and under another tenant
expected_results: only tenant's active projects returned; other tenant's rows never appear; %{results, meta} shape

test_cases.name: non-allowlisted field is rejected
preconditions: a projects entity where secret_field is NOT filterable
expected_results: {:error, _} — rejected, no query executed; secret_field never queried

test_cases.name: SQL-injection payload is treated as a literal value
expected_results: matches zero rows (literal comparison); no error leaking SQL; no extra rows returned

test_cases.name: pagination is capped
expected_results: result length <= configured max page size; meta.total_count reflects the full count

test_cases.name: body/param cannot override tenant scope
preconditions: tenant_t scope; rows exist under tenant_u
expected_results: scope stays tenant_t; tenant_u rows never returned

technical_notes: Module: Loopctl.ContextRetriever.Executor. Build Ecto queries dynamically from the entity allowlist via field references (e.g. dynamic/2 with validated field atoms from the entity, NOT from raw strings), values always as pinned params.
SECURITY: never String.to_atom on model input; map a validated allowlisted field name to a known atom/column; reject anything else. No fragment/raw SQL with interpolated values.
Tenant predicate is mandatory and non-overridable; run on the repo the backing source uses (OLTP Loopctl.Repo for projects/stories).
Full-text: reuse loopctl's existing parameterized keyword/full-text approach (the articles search path is the reference) rather than raw ILIKE string-building.
Return only entity-declared fields; do not select * into the response.
Tests use Loopctl.Fixtures.fixture/2 with real projects/stories rows across two tenants.
